title: Multiplying and dividing decimals
blurb: Multiply decimals by counting decimal places, divide by moving the point until the divisor is whole, and shift the point for powers of 10.
question: Each tablet holds 0.125 mg of a drug. How many milligrams are in 6 tablets, and how many 0.25 mg doses can be made from a 4.5 mg supply?

teach.h: Whole-number work, then place the point
teach.body: Formally, a decimal product has as many decimal places as its factors have in total, and a quotient is unchanged when the dividend and divisor are both multiplied by the same power of 10. In plain English: multiply as if the points were not there and then count places; to divide, slide both points right until the divisor is a whole number. Estimate first so a misplaced point jumps out.

items: Count decimal places in the factors: 1 (in 2.4) + 1 (in 1.5) = 2.
Place the point 2 places from the right: 3.60 = 3.6. Estimate: 2 × 2 = 4, close to 3.6. ✓
0.3 × 0.02: 3 × 2 = 6, and 1 + 2 = 3 places, so 0.006. Fill empty places with zeros.

teach.h: Count the places in both factors
head: Problem
Places
Product
teach.caption: Count places BEFORE dropping any end zeros: 25 × 12 = 300, and 2 places gives 3.00.
Moving both points the same number of places keeps the answer the same.

items: The divisor 1.2 has 1 decimal place. Move both points 1 place right: 75.6 ÷ 12.
Divide: 12 goes into 75 six times (72), remainder 3; bring down 6 to get 36; 12 goes into 36 three times.
Put the point straight above its place in 75.6: the answer is 6.3.

teach.h: Powers of 10 just move the point
Check the size before you choose
teach.body: Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes the result smaller: 8 × 0.5 = 4. Dividing by a number less than 1 makes it larger: 8 ÷ 0.5 = 16. So 48 ÷ 0.8 must be more than 48 (it is 60), and 6.3 × 0.05 must be much less than 6.3 (it is 0.315). Most misplaced-point options fail this one-second check.

teach.text: Decimal slips the HESI A2 builds wrong answers from: 0.3 × 0.2 = 0.06, not 0.6 (count BOTH factors' places), and 4.5 ÷ 0.15 = 30, not 0.3 (move the dividend's point as well as the divisor's).

teach.h: Scenario: Andre checks a tablet supply
teach.body: Andre Williams, a pharmacy-technician applicant, needs the drug in 6 tablets of 0.125 mg: 125 × 6 = 750, and 0.125 has 3 places, so 0.750 = 0.75 mg. Then he finds how many 0.25 mg doses a 4.5 mg supply makes: move both points 2 places, 450 ÷ 25 = 18 doses. Checks: 6 tablets of about 0.1 mg is about 0.6 mg, close to 0.75 ✓; 18 × 0.25 = 4.5 ✓.

items: Multiply: multiply as whole numbers, then give the product as many decimal places as both factors combined.
Divide: move the divisor's point to make it whole, and move the dividend's point the same number of places.
× or ÷ by 10, 100, 1,000: move the point 1, 2, 3 places (right to multiply, left to divide).
Size check: × by less than 1 shrinks; ÷ by less than 1 grows.

summary: You can now multiply decimals by counting places, divide by a decimal by making the divisor whole, and move the point for powers of 10. You also size-check every answer, which exposes the misplaced-point options the HESI A2 offers.

A.q: Ground turkey costs $4.85 per pound. What is the cost of 2.6 pounds?
A.why: 485 × 26 = 12,610. The factors have 2 + 1 = 3 decimal places, so 12.610 = $12.61. Estimate: 5 × 2.6 = 13. ✓

whyNot.0: $126.10 places the point after only 2 decimal places instead of 3.
whyNot.1: $9.70 is the cost of 2 pounds only; the 0.6 pound is missing.
whyNot.3: $1.26 places the point 4 places from the right, one place too many.

A.q: A pharmacist divides 6.3 g of powder into doses of 0.45 g each. How many doses does this make?

whyNot.0: 1.4 moves the divisor's point only 1 place (6.3 ÷ 4.5).
whyNot.2: 140 moves the dividend's point one place more than the divisor's.
whyNot.3: 0.14 moves the divisor's point but not the dividend's (6.3 ÷ 45).

B.why: The divisor has 3 decimal places. Move both points 3 places: 840 ÷ 7 = 120. Check: 120 × 0.007 = 0.84.

whyNot.0: 12 moves the dividend's point only 2 places (84 ÷ 7) while the divisor's moved 3.
whyNot.1: 1,200 moves the dividend's point 4 places, one more than the divisor's.
whyNot.2: 0.12 divides 0.84 by 7 without moving the dividend's point.

B.q: A nursing assistant earns $17.40 per hour. How much does she earn for a 6.5-hour shift?
B.why: 1740 × 65 = 113,100. The factors have 2 + 1 = 3 decimal places: 113.100 = $113.10. Estimate: 17 × 6.5 ≈ 110. ✓

whyNot.0: $11.31 places the point one place too far left.
whyNot.2: $104.40 pays 6 hours and drops the half hour.
whyNot.3: $121.80 rounds the shift up to 7 hours.

whyNot.0: 0.003 moves the divisor's point but not the dividend's (0.036 ÷ 12).
whyNot.3: 0.3 moves the dividend's point 2 places while the divisor's moved 1.

C.q: A nursing assistant earns $17.40 per hour and $26.10 per hour for overtime. Last week she worked 40 regular hours and 6.5 overtime hours. How much did she earn?

whyNot.1: $809.10 pays all 46.5 hours at the regular rate of $17.40.
whyNot.3: $712.97 misplaces the point in the overtime pay (16.965 instead of 169.65).

C.q: Brand A saline wipes cost $3.48 for 12 ounces. Brand B costs $5.40 for 20 ounces. Which is the better buy, and by how much per ounce?
C.why: Unit prices: A = 3.48 ÷ 12 = $0.29 per ounce; B = 5.40 ÷ 20 = $0.27 per ounce. B is cheaper by 0.29 − 0.27 = $0.02 per ounce.

whyNot.0: A costs $0.29 per ounce, more than B's $0.27, so A is not the better buy.
whyNot.2: B is cheaper, but the difference is 0.02, not 0.20; the point has slipped one place.
whyNot.3: This inverts the rate: 12 ÷ 3.48 ≈ 3.45 and 20 ÷ 5.40 ≈ 3.70 are ounces per dollar, where the HIGHER number is the better buy, and their difference is not a price.

C.q: A 2.25 L bag is split into 0.15 L portions, and each portion costs $0.85 to prepare. What is the total cost?

whyNot.0: $1.28 moves the dividend's point only 1 place (1.5 portions), then 1.5 × 0.85 = 1.275.
whyNot.1: $1.91 multiplies the liters by the cost per portion (2.25 × 0.85) and skips finding the number of portions.
whyNot.2: $127.50 moves the dividend's point 3 places (150 portions) while the divisor's moved 2.

reteach.title: Decimals are dollars and cents
reteach.question: How does thinking in cents make the decimal rules for multiplying and dividing obvious?

blocks.h: A part of a part is small
blocks.body: Multiplying by a decimal takes a part of something. 0.3 of $0.20 is 3 tenths of 20 cents, which is 6 cents: $0.06. A part of a part is smaller than both parts, which is why 0.3 × 0.2 has more decimal places (2) than either factor. Dividing asks how many fit: how many 15-cent stamps can $4.50 buy?

head: Question
In dollars
In cents
blocks.caption: Changing both amounts to cents changes the numbers, not the answer.

items: Going from dollars to cents multiplies BOTH amounts by 100: both points move 2 places.
If you changed only the price to cents (4.50 ÷ 15), you would be comparing dollars with cents.
That mismatch is exactly the move-only-the-divisor slip.

blocks.text: $4.50 buys 30 stamps at 15 cents, not 0.3 of a stamp. If the answer looks absurd in cents, a point was moved in only one number.

explain.body: Multiply as if there were no points, then count the decimal places in BOTH factors and give the answer that many places. 1.25 × 0.8: 125 × 8 = 1,000, and 2 + 1 = 3 places, so 1.000 = 1.

test.why: 125 × 8 = 1,000. Three decimal places in total gives 1.000 = 1. Estimate: 1.25 is a bit more than 1, and 0.8 of it is about 1. ✓

whyNot.1: 0.1 places the point 4 places from the right, one too many.
whyNot.2: 10 places the point after only 2 decimal places.
whyNot.3: 0.01 places the point 5 places from the right.

explain.body: Move the divisor's point right until it is a whole number, then move the dividend's point the same number of places. 9.6 ÷ 0.32 becomes 960 ÷ 32.

whyNot.0: 3 moves the dividend only 1 place (96 ÷ 32) while the divisor moved 2.
whyNot.2: 300 moves the dividend 3 places, one more than the divisor.
whyNot.3: 0.3 moves the divisor's point but not the dividend's (9.6 ÷ 32 = 0.3).

explain.body: Multiplying by 10, 100 or 1,000 moves the point 1, 2 or 3 places right; dividing moves it left. Count the zeros, move that many places.

test.q: Each of 1,000 tablets contains 0.025 g of a drug. How many grams of the drug are in all the tablets together?
test.why: × 1,000 moves the point 3 places right: 0.025 → 25 g.

whyNot.0: 2.5 g moves the point only 2 places (× 100).
whyNot.2: 0.25 g moves the point only 1 place (× 10).

explain.body: Dividing by a number less than 1 gives a result LARGER than the number you started with; multiplying by it gives a SMALLER result. Use this to rule out misplaced points.

test.q: Without working it out exactly, which statement about 48 ÷ 0.8 is true?
test.why: 0.8 is less than 1, so more than 48 of them fit into 48: 48 ÷ 0.8 = 480 ÷ 8 = 60.

whyNot.0: Dividing by a number less than 1 makes the result larger, not smaller.
whyNot.2: 48 × 0.8 = 38.4; multiplying and dividing by 0.8 give different results.
whyNot.3: A result less than 1 would come from 0.8 ÷ 48, the division reversed.
